voyage.title: The Travels of Marco Polo (1271-1295)
voyage.ships: overland by caravan, and home by sea from Zaiton
voyage.sponsor: travelling with his father and uncle, merchants of Venice
voyage.summary: Twenty-four years out of Venice: through Persia and the Pamirs to Kublai Khan's court at Khanbaliq, years in the Khan's service across Cathay and the south, then home by sea through the Indies, Ceylon and Hormuz.
voyage.what_was_lost: Polo kept no journal. The book was dictated in a Genoese prison around 1298 to Rustichello of Pisa, a writer of Arthurian romances, more than two decades after the events. No original manuscript survives and the roughly 150 that do disagree with one another, some carrying episodes the others lack.

waypoints.event: Marco Polo, along with his father Nicolo and uncle Maffeo, returned to Venice after their journey to Acre and Jerusalem, before setting out again for the court of the grand khan.
waypoints.diary_source_citation: The Travels of Marco Polo, the Venetian (trans. William Marsden, rev. ed. 1892)

waypoints.event: The Polos returned to Acre from Venice, bringing young Marco Polo with them; under the sanction of the papal legate they visited Jerusalem to obtain oil from the lamp of the holy sepulchre as directed by the grand khan, then returned to Acre before proceeding onward.
waypoints.diary_source_citation: The Travels of Marco Polo, the Venetian (trans. William Marsden, rev. ed. 1892)

waypoints.event: Marco Polo's party, after crossing a desert region famous for its wild asses, arrived at the kingdom of Kierman (ancient Karmania) on the southern route through Persia, a land noted for its fossil and mineral productions and manufactures.
waypoints.diary_source_citation: The Travels of Marco Polo, the Venetian (trans. William Marsden, rev. ed. 1892)

waypoints.event: Marco Polo and his party traveled through Persian Irak, Khorasan, and the city of Balkh into the country of Badakhshan, near the sources of the Oxus, where they remained for about twelve months, possibly due to Marco's illness or the need to wait for a caravan escort before crossing the mountains.
waypoints.diary_source_citation: The Travels of Marco Polo, the Venetian (trans. William Marsden, rev. ed. 1892)

waypoints.place_modern: Pamir Plateau (Roof of the World), Tajikistan/Afghanistan border region
waypoints.event: After leaving Vokhan (Wakhan) and ascending for three days through mountain after mountain, Marco Polo's party reached the elevated plateau where the surrounding summits seemed the highest lands in the world, finding a large lake feeding a river that ran through a lush plain.
waypoints.diary_source_citation: The Travels of Marco Polo, the Venetian (trans. William Marsden, rev. ed. 1892)

waypoints.event: Marco Polo's party reached Kashcar, a large and prosperous city under the dominion of the grand khan, whose Muslim inhabitants subsisted by commerce and manufacturing, especially cotton goods, and cultivated gardens, orchards, and vineyards.
waypoints.diary_source_citation: The Travels of Marco Polo, the Venetian (trans. William Marsden, rev. ed. 1892)

waypoints.place_modern: Lop Nur region / Ruoqiang, Xinjiang, China
waypoints.event: Marco Polo describes arriving at the city of Lop on the edge of the great desert, where travelers rested and provisioned themselves with camels and a month's supply of food before crossing the desert of Lop.
waypoints.diary_source_citation: The Travels of Marco Polo, the Venetian (trans. William Marsden, rev. ed. 1892)

waypoints.event: Marco Polo describes arriving at Kampion, the principal city of the province of Tanguth, noting its size and magnificence and its jurisdiction over the whole province, as well as the mix of idolaters, Muslims, and Christians living there.
waypoints.diary_source_citation: The Travels of Marco Polo, the Venetian (trans. William Marsden, rev. ed. 1892)

waypoints.event: Marco Polo describes arriving at the city of Shaudu, built by Kublai Khan, where the Great Khan had constructed a magnificent marble palace enclosed within a sixteen-mile walled park.
waypoints.diary_source_citation: The Travels of Marco Polo, the Venetian (trans. William Marsden, rev. ed. 1892)

waypoints.event: After a year-long journey delayed by snow and flooded rivers, Niccolò, Maffeo, and Marco Polo arrived at the imperial residence of the Great Khan Kublai in Cathay (northern China), where they were received and honored at his court.
waypoints.diary_source_citation: The Travels of Marco Polo, the Venetian (trans. William Marsden, rev. ed. 1892)

waypoints.event: Marco Polo describes reaching the city of Mien, capital of the kingdom, after a fifteen-day journey through depopulated forests full of elephants and rhinoceroses, following the Great Khan's conquest of the territories of the king of Bangala and Mien.
waypoints.diary_source_citation: The Travels of Marco Polo, the Venetian (trans. William Marsden, rev. ed. 1892)

waypoints.event: Marco Polo describes reaching the noble and magnificent city of Kin-sai, whose name signifies 'the celestial city,' noting its unmatched grandeur, beauty, and abundant delights, and recounts that he visited it frequently and recorded detailed observations about it.
waypoints.diary_source_citation: The Travels of Marco Polo, the Venetian (trans. William Marsden, rev. ed. 1892)

waypoints.event: Marco Polo and his companions, escorting a Mongol princess to Persia, departed China from the great port of Zai-tun in the province of Fo-kien, a city famed for its trade with India and its rich merchandise.
waypoints.diary_source_citation: The Travels of Marco Polo, the Venetian (trans. William Marsden, rev. ed. 1892)

waypoints.place_modern: Coast of Central Vietnam (former Champa kingdom, near Qui Nhon)
waypoints.event: On the return voyage escorting the Mongol princess, the fleet carrying Marco Polo passed along the coast of Cochin-China and touched at the country of Tsiampa (Champa), a land Marco Polo notes he had previously visited in 1280.
waypoints.diary_source_citation: The Travels of Marco Polo, the Venetian (trans. William Marsden, rev. ed. 1892)

waypoints.event: On the homeward voyage from China, Marco Polo's fleet reached the island the Venetians called Java Minor (identified by the editor as Sumatra), landing on its north-eastern coast where they were forced to remain for five months awaiting favourable winds to cross the Bay of Bengal.
waypoints.diary_source_citation: The Travels of Marco Polo, the Venetian (trans. William Marsden, rev. ed. 1892)

waypoints.event: Marco Polo describes the kingdom of Malabar on the western coast of Greater India as an independent realm with its own king and language, noting astronomical observations (the height of the north star) and the danger posed by pirate fleets operating along that coast and neighboring Guzzerat.
waypoints.diary_source_citation: The Travels of Marco Polo, the Venetian (trans. William Marsden, rev. ed. 1892)

waypoints.event: After an eighteen-month voyage through the Indian seas escorting the Mongol princess, the Polo party's fleet made landfall at Hormuz, where they learned that Arghun, the king for whom the princess had been intended as bride, had died, and that the kingdom was ruled by a regent while Arghun's son Ghazan awaited his chance to claim the throne.
waypoints.diary_source_citation: The Travels of Marco Polo, the Venetian (trans. William Marsden, rev. ed. 1892)

waypoints.event: Returning from their long sojourn in the Mongol court, Marco Polo and his father and uncle reached the Black Sea port of Trebizond, from which they continued via Constantinople and Negropont to Venice, completing a twenty-four-year absence.
waypoints.diary_source_citation: The Travels of Marco Polo, the Venetian (trans. William Marsden, rev. ed. 1892)

waypoints.event: After twenty-four years away, Nicolo, Maffeo, and Marco Polo finally arrived back in their native city of Venice, having traveled from Trebizond through Constantinople and Negropont; their relatives initially failed to recognize them.
waypoints.diary_source_citation: The Travels of Marco Polo, the Venetian (trans. William Marsden, rev. ed. 1892)
